why: The two N/A branches of the rule, one per folder. `pass/` has `src/app.ts` — real TypeScript — and NO package.json: with no manifest there is no script to invoke, and the rule asks for a target CI can call. `fail/` has the package.json and no .ts or .tsx file at all: charging a project that has no types for a type check is accusing by vocabulary. The presence of TypeScript on the side with no manifest is deliberate, and it is what makes each folder isolate ONE branch: without it the `pass` side would be N/A for two reasons at once, and the mutation of either one would still find the other in front of it. Each branch has to be the only path on its side, or the proof does not say which of them locked.
